summary: RELAY is a tool that helps figure out the best way to communicate in space. It looks at how planets, satellites, and space stations move and uses that info to plan the best paths for messages to travel. Users can pick from pre-set locations or enter their own coordinates to define specific points in space. As the planets and stars move, RELAY updates the positions in real-time, so users can see how it affects communication between different spots. By studying these movements, RELAY aims to help find the best spots to relay messages and plan reliable communication networks for future missions to other planets, space stations, and even settlements on other worlds. This can be really useful for planning things like trips to Mars or setting up a base on the moon.
details:
Project Overview - RELAY: Finding the Best Spot for Space Communication Relays

RELAY is a tool that helps figure out the best way to communicate between different places in space. It's a big job to keep talking to each other when you're on different planets, satellites, or space stations, because everything is always moving. So, RELAY uses special math and data about where things are in space to plan the best communication routes. You can pick from some common places, like near Mars or between Earth and the Sun, or you can put in your own coordinates to find a specific spot. It even works for places on planets, using latitude and longitude. The system gets its information from NASA, so it's always up to date, and it can change the coordinates as time goes on. This way, RELAY can help people communicate clearly and reliably, even when they're really far apart in space.

When we think about living on other planets, we need to figure out how to stay in touch with each other. This is a tough problem because of how far apart we'll be and how planets move. RELAY is a tool that helps us understand and plan ways to communicate across huge distances. As we start to build homes on other planets, we'll face big challenges like delays in talking to each other and dealing with changing positions in space. RELAY helps us tackle these issues by finding the best spots to put relays, which are like messengers that help us stay connected. The goal is to make communication in space more reliable, so we can explore, travel, and even live on other planets with ease.

This project is a mix of web development, space mechanics, and astronomy data handling. It uses NASA's Horizons API to get the exact positions of stars and planets, and does complex math to figure out where things are in space. The whole thing is put online using Vercel, so you can access it from any browser.

What's unique about RELAY is how it brings together actual space data and a interactive tool for planning communication. Instead of just thinking of space communication as a straightforward link between two points, it takes into account the fact that celestial bodies and orbits are always on the move. This means the platform can be used in different situations, thanks to its ability to mix and match pre-set orbit plans with custom coordinates. It's pretty flexible, which is handy for different mission scenarios.

When the team was working on this project, they thought about a lot of things, like how accurate the positions would be, how things in space are always changing, and if the data they had was reliable. They also wanted to make sure the tool could work with different orbits and was easy to use. The main goal was to create something that would really work, be useful for a lot of people, and help connect the ideas of how things move in space and how we communicate with them. This could help solve some of the big problems we'll face as we try to explore and live beyond Earth.
